description:
Purpose: Reproduce the reported reliability problems. Define one portable identity, command, context and selection contract.

Current state: this phase is planned; current production persistence remains JSON until the SQLite/API migration is implemented. Reuse existing capabilities instead of creating another planner.

Deliverables and sole owners:
- P116(F025)/T461: Reproducible baseline fixtures for the six reported failures and the new storage boundary.
- P116(F025)/T462: One domain contract for identity, eligibility, context, phase continuity and revision-aware results.

Execution contract:
Follow the task dependencies and the phase priority in the rebuilt F025 plan. Keep coherent phase work and recover approved detours; do not introduce a global task queue or silently preempt active work. Use the user-scoped service/SQLite boundary, explicit workspace identity, complete bounded context and revision-bound evidence wherever applicable.

Acceptance:
Each task proves its stated outcome; preserve IDs/history, single-owner decisions and phase handoffs. Mechanical parent/dependency effects are consistent; semantic review is factual, reviewed-unchanged or explicitly pending. Native/provider/installed claims need their actual owner evidence.

tasks.title: Reproduce the reliability failures on isolated fixtures
tasks.description:
Outcome: Reproducible baseline fixtures for the six reported failures and the new storage boundary.

Current implementation: Handoffs, rules, claims, read tracking and recommendation already exist. Reports identify unreliable behavior; previous fixture reports do not certify this checkout.

Implementation responsibility:
- Build isolated old-format fixtures for several handoffs, repeated resume reads, ignored conventions, nested detours, current-phase priority bias and duplicate capability creation.
- Capture real core/MCP/Pi/server outputs and exact revisions, including same-task races, source workspace inference and failed/incomplete replies.
- Record bytes, characters, tool calls and model tokens where available; define comparable small/large-plan and no-op fixtures for later regression.
- Add the descriptor-missing/incompatible, missing-HOME and per-project-server assumptions to the migration baseline without changing real data.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Each reported case has a reproducible input and an observable expected correction; uncertain causes stay explicit.
- Fixtures use mkdtemp and stop owned processes; no real project is migrated or dashboard auto-started.
- Measurements distinguish product scenarios from synthetic SQL primitives.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped: reproducible baseline for the six reported reliability failures and the migration storage boundary, in four runnable suites (26 tests, all green) plus a checked-in measurement snapshot. Core (packages/plan-core/test/agent-brain-baseline.test.mjs, 16 tests): several handoffs surface as unranked competing claims with old-format phase-file read-back; repeated resume reads (fresh session needs task+phase+feature, unrelated writes stale persisted attestations); ignored conventions (unread guidelines never gate an eligible start; customized planner skill preserved, never reconciled); nested detours resolve LIFO one level at a time with standardized resume proposals; current-phase priority bias (currentPhaseId overrides global priority with no session-ownership check — AB-IMP-007; higher-priority empty phase silently skipped with no planning claim — AB-IMP-008); duplicate capability creation (managed skills idempotent, legacy copies adopted); same-task claim race between two PlanStore instances; failed/incomplete reply paths; migration boundary (descriptor missing = workspace undetectable, schemaVersion 999 rejected, legacy features.json migrates). MCP (packages/plan-mcp/test/agent-brain-baseline-mcp.test.mjs, 4 tests, real published server over stdio): same-task race between two sessions (one started=true, loser denied); readable failures for unknown task/phase and defined reply for incomplete args; source workspace inference captured live (AGENT_PLAN_ROOT unset -> cwd/.planner); scripted resume scenario measured at 6 tool calls, 1723 text bytes, 6699 structured bytes (~4x duplication) plus the REQUIREMENTS_READ_REQUIRED extra read per start. Server (packages/plan-server/test/agent-brain-baseline-server.test.mjs, 4 tests, real HTTP): per-project server isolation; same-task start race through POST /tasks/:id/start (one 200, one refusal 400, exactly one active owner); shaped failures for unknown entity and invalid write; missing-HOME evidence (empty HOME yields empty homedir() without throwing — user-scope installs must fail explicitly). Measurements (packages/plan-core/test/agent-brain-baseline-measurements.test.mjs + docs/agent-brain/baseline/measurements.json): no-op/small/large product scenarios (0/27/632 entities) — recommendation reply is size-bounded (1560 bytes at both 27 and 632 entities, claims capped at 8) while the full recommendation object grows (4566 -> 10341 bytes); model tokens recorded null as an explicit open boundary. Full narrative with expected corrections, uncertain causes and unverified boundaries: docs/agent-brain/baseline/README.md. Verification: all four suites green locally (26/26); no real project touched, mkdtemp isolation, owned processes stopped, no dashboard started. Exact revisions: feat/agent-brain @ 59f9028059e3b6206dd2545ec405f6fdc8d139e1, core/mcp/server 0.4.11. Remaining: none (Pi-adapter-level capture and model-token accounting stay model-visible, recorded as unverified boundaries).
tasks.notes: Post-completion environment repair (2026-11-15, user-verified gap): pnpm-workspace.yaml was left malformed by another session (duplicated packages/agent-brain-web-ui entries plus a corrupted line; the referenced package directory does not exist), which broke pnpm run dev while T461 was already marked done. Repair: restored the file to its valid original form (packages/* only). Verification after repair: pnpm run dev healthy in background — plan-server listening on http://127.0.0.1:3090 (plan root /Users/antonio/projects/agent-plan/.planner), Vite dev on http://localhost:5175 proxying to it; curl checks returned 200 on the Vite root and a real project payload from /api/v1/project. The 26 baseline tests remain green. Process correction recorded: before declaring a task done, sanity-check the workspace environment (workspace YAML, install, build), not only the task's own tests.

tasks.title: Define one shared next-work and context contract
tasks.description:
Outcome: One domain contract for identity, eligibility, context, phase continuity and revision-aware results.

Current implementation: Selection/read-order and adapter messages diverge. The accepted target is HOME SQLite behind a single application service, while current consumers still open JSON stores.

Implementation responsibility:
- Specify stable project/repository/workspace/caller/native-session/execution identities and the boundaries implemented by T489, the SQLite task and T490.
- Define owned active work and valid returns before globally ready feature -> phase -> task ordering. Preserve coherent phase work; no global task queue or automatic priority preemption.
- Define typed success/non-success, actual context delivery, retained-context restoration, role-aware API parity and source/target availability extension points.
- Map every baseline case to one implementation owner and define bounded mutation/resume/query/editor budgets with explicit continuation.

Acceptance and evidence:
- Core/MCP/Pi/server/UI can consume the same versioned result shapes.
- Dependency readiness is distinct from desired ordering and code/rationale relationships.
- Phase continuity does not add an unapproved global exclusive phase lock; the warning-only no-task guard remains.
